source.title: Flat Seeking Bayesian Neural Networks
source.authors: Van-Anh Nguyen; Tung-Long Vuong; Hoang Phan; Thanh-Toan Do; Dinh Q. Phung; Trung Le

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the paper and supplementary material through page 24; no cut-off or garbling affecting the reported experiments is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly compares a sharpness-aware posterior with baseline Bayesian neural networks, reports generalization-related metrics and sharpness results, and qualifies the relationship between flatness and generalization. Its task is improving BNNs, not the claim versions' interventions, so it refines the flatness/generalization connection without testing most mapped versions.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the study's flat versus non-flat BNN comparisons on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, its stated CIFAR-10-C aggregate results, and sharpness/Hessian measurements. Baseline results sourced from Maddox et al. and bSAM results sourced from Möllenhoff and Khan are not treated as this study's own tested results. The CIFAR-10-C aggregate table reports separate corruption groups and an overall average; retained as aggregate rows. Tables 1–3 contain separately reported method/model/dataset results; all applicable result rows are included.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization premise to develop a Bayesian training method and evaluates its predictive performance. It does not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure, its relationship to train–test error gaps, or its ranking against other measures. Its Euclidean sharpness and Hessian measurements concern different constructs. No other claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they argue that sharpness-aware posteriors yield flatter sampled models and better ensemble predictive performance and average corruption robustness. Qualify the metric claim: improvements are not universal. For example, Table 1 PreResNet-164 SWAG NLL worsens from 0.6595 to 0.6704, WideResNet28x10 SWAG ECE worsens from 0.0113 to 0.0196, and Table 4 DenseNet-161 SGLD ECE worsens from 0.0157 to 0.0166. The study does not establish V7's specific sharpness–gap relationship.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a sharpness-aware Bayesian posterior and integrates it into BNN methods; the claim versions concern standard supervised-network generalization, capacity and measurement relationships, not this posterior intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by baseline method, architecture, dataset and metric. On CIFAR-10-C, accuracy differs by corruption group; reported averages conceal some group-level decreases.

fits_no_version.finding: Sharpness-aware BNN variants improve reported ensemble accuracy across the tested CIFAR and ImageNet comparisons; this evaluates the proposed method.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness-aware posterior training can improve Bayesian ensemble classification accuracy on image benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: F-SWAG has lower reported Euclidean loss sharpness than SWAG; flat variants also have lower log largest Hessian eigenvalues. The Deep-ensemble eigenvalue ratio increases, and the SWAG ratio is unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness-aware Bayesian training can reduce unscaled loss sharpness and largest Hessian eigenvalues, without uniformly reducing Hessian eigenvalue ratios.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 5 shows improved average CIFAR-10-C calibration and accuracy, with accuracy decreases in some corruption groups. Several extracted accuracy pairs name the wrong method.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness-aware Bayesian training can improve average corruption performance while producing mixed accuracy changes across corruption groups.

record.problems: The study evaluates BNN ensemble metrics rather than train-test error gaps. Some baselines are sourced from earlier work rather than rerun, and several table values in the supplied flattened text cannot be assigned confidently. ImageNet results have no reported error bars. The main sharpness comparison referenced in supplementary material does not include the referenced numerical scores in the supplied text. The measured Hessian curvature does not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or its association with generalization gaps.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row cap. Some Table 3 and Table 2 cells are not reliably assignable from the supplied flattened layout and are represented as cannot_determine rather than reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD performance under limited or broader tuning. Using different optimizers for different BNN methods is not a controlled optimizer comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epochs and adaptations that recover performance.
Adding or removing dropout, small-data effects, excessive dropout, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal. MC-Dropout versus F-MC-Dropout changes sharpness-aware training.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with train–test error gaps among similarly fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Geometry-aware training and unscaled sharpness/Hessian measurements do not establish these.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine with respect to the supplied claim versions, because no row measures a version's effect; this does not deny the reported method-performance gains. These comparisons should be retained as findings outside the versions rather than claim-test rows. Missing is empty because no unrecorded result tests a supplied version. The supplied supplementary text contains additional method evaluations, including the L2 ablation and computational costs, but these do not bear on the versions.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep past interpolation or test-error versus width measurement.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD for generalization.
No large versus small batch comparison.
Dropout appears as a BNN baseline, but the study does not test whether adding/removing dropout changes test error as stated in this version.
Does not test magnitude-aware sharpness or rank it against norm- and margin-based measures; the reported sharpness is unscaled Euclidean perturbation and the Hessian largest eigenvalue.
